title: a `neural_block` descriptor with an empty `kernel` value is rejected — its wire identity must be non-empty
why: This check was minted in both
clauses (C++ `_validate_neural_block`'s first line; Python's mirror) but
never got a corpus row or a named test — grep-verified across both
test trees before this fixture existed. It is wire-reachable,
cross-language, and carries an identical substring, exactly the corpus's
class of claim.
Fixture content is row01's golden with the top-level `kernel` VALUE
emptied (the key stays present, satisfying C++ `parse_sidecar`'s
structural key requirement, so this row tests the neural clause's own
non-emptiness check, not the parse-time key-presence one row17 pins).
KEY ORDER stays LOAD-BEARING here too: `forward_exec` and
`vjp_exec` still precede the top-level `kernel`, so the masking fix must
still correctly resolve the (now-empty) top-level `kernel` value rather
than a nested exec object's own literal 'kernel' text.
This is the FIRST check inside the `neural_block` clause in both
languages, run before the scalar_type / arg_spec / requiredness checks —
the descriptor's wire identity is validated before anything else about
its shape, which this row's otherwise-golden content proves by reaching
exactly this check and no other.
`host_add_plugin` is exercised too: its only structural gate is the
shared validator.
